questions.text: How many people work in the business, including contractors who use your systems?
Does the Privacy Act 1988 cover your business?
questions.help: Most businesses with annual turnover of A$3 million or less are outside it. Health service providers, businesses that trade in personal information and Commonwealth contractors are covered at any size, and there are other exceptions. The AU Frameworks Check works this out in detail.

options.label: Yes, our turnover is over A$3 million
Yes, at any size: we provide a health service, trade in personal information or hold a Commonwealth contract
No, our turnover is A$3 million or less and none of those apply

questions.text: Which AI tools do staff use for work, approved or not?
questions.help: Pick every one you know or suspect is in use. AI built into software you already pay for counts too.

options.label: Coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor or Claude Code
AI features inside software we already use, such as writing, design or notes tools
AI browser extensions or meeting note-taker bots

questions.text: When staff use these tools for work, which accounts do they sign in with?
questions.help: A personal account is one a person signs up for with any email, free or paid. A business account sits in a workspace the business pays for and administers.

options.label: Business or enterprise accounts the business pays for and administers
A mix of business accounts and staff's own accounts
Mostly staff's own free or paid accounts

questions.text: Do staff pay for AI subscriptions themselves?

options.label: Yes, and some claim them as expenses
Yes, some pay out of their own pocket

questions.text: Do AI note-takers or recording bots join your calls and meetings?

options.label: Yes, one tool the business set up

questions.text: Which of these could staff be putting into AI tools?

options.label: Customer or client personal information, such as names, contact details or case notes
Financial details, such as bank, card or tax file numbers
Source code, passwords or API keys
Confidential business information, such as contracts, pricing or plans
None of these, as far as we know

questions.text: Do client contracts or confidentiality agreements limit where you can send client information?
Do you have a written AI use policy?

options.label: Yes, and staff have read and accepted it
Yes, but not all staff have seen it, or it is out of date

questions.text: Is there a list of the AI tools staff may use, and for what?

options.label: Yes, a written list we keep current
Informally, people know what is allowed

questions.text: If someone wants a new AI tool, how do they get it approved?

options.label: There is a set way and we answer within about a week
There is a set way, but it is slow

questions.text: Is one person responsible for how the business uses AI?
Have staff been shown what they may and may not put into AI tools?

options.label: Yes, all staff in the last 12 months

questions.text: If someone used an AI tool the business has not approved, how would you find out?

options.label: Our network, device or browser controls block or flag it
We review expense claims, sign-ups or sign-in logs

questions.text: Do you keep a register of the AI tools in use, with an owner and the data each one handles?

options.label: Yes, but it is out of date

questions.text: For the business AI accounts you have, have you checked the training, retention and sharing settings?

options.label: Not yet, or only on some
We have no business AI accounts

questions.text: When someone leaves, can you remove their access to AI tools and the work data in them?

options.label: Yes, we switch off their business accounts
No, or the work sits in their own accounts
